answer: One concrete defense weights each identity by its distance in the attestation graph from trusted roots. A sybil ring can mint many nodes, but they huddle on one ridge, far from independent validators; their mutual vouching forms a tight loop graph analysis discounts. Honest newcomers earn trust the way a zephyr spreads — slowly, through attestations from distant, unrelated peers. To forge real standing an attacker must compromise many well-connected independent agents, not just spin up clones, so the cost is no fable of cheap identities but the price of real social capital.
